title: Three accounts, one book
subtitle: How much sits behind one company, one industry, one country and one currency
note: The example is Antevo's model book: one household that spends in francs, with three accounts named Capital Preservation, Balanced and Growth. Amounts are left out; shares of the whole are shown. Companies are described, not named. Every figure is an Antevo engine's answer on the date shown.

tries.label: The book, piece by piece
tries.source: Antevo Wealth, Tremor Watch and Executive Brief, 25 Nov 2026. Shares are added up from the positions the engine returned; a fund counts as one holding.

items.name: One company
evidence: The largest holding, a US phone and device maker, is 17.3% of the whole and sits in all three accounts
The three US technology shares (the device maker, a software company and a chip designer) make 40.7% together
Nine holdings in all: the largest five make 71.5%

items.name: One industry
evidence: Technology 48%, everyday consumer goods 14.1%, financials 12.6%, health care 9.9%
The industry is known for 84.6% of the book; the other 15.4% is a short-dated US government bond fund
A US bank share (8.4%) and a US bank fund (4.2%) are the same industry twice

items.name: One country, one currency
evidence: 85.9% of the book is in the United States and priced in dollars; 14.1% is in Switzerland
The Swiss share is one food company, not a spread of Swiss companies
The household spends in francs: a move in the dollar moves 86% of the book

items.name: The names on the accounts
evidence: Five of the nine holdings sit in all three accounts, in different weights
A replay of the 2000 to 2002 crash: Capital Preservation −34%, Balanced −46%, Growth −61%
A replay of a past event, not a forecast

items.name: Cash when needed
evidence: Every position is a listed share or fund: the engine counts 100% as sellable within a day
Bonds are 15.4% of the book, shares 84.6%

steps.label: What is worth a look, with the links

items.do: Add each holding up across every account before judging any one account
items.why: Five of the nine holdings sit in all three accounts, so no single statement shows the real share.

items.do: Look inside any fund you hold
items.why: A US bank fund sits beside a US bank share here: a fund can double a holding you already have. The engine counts a fund as one holding and does not look inside it.

items.do: Write down the share you are at ease with behind one company, one industry and one currency
items.why: The page shows where the book stands; where the line sits is for you and your adviser.

items.do: See how each account fared in past crashes
items.why: A name on an account says what was intended; a replay says what the holdings did.

items.do: Note the dates that touch what you hold
items.why: On 25 November the chip designer (8.6% of the book) reports after the US close, the day the US inflation figure is due.

items.do: Read it again after a big market day
items.why: Shares of the whole move with prices: a holding that rises becomes a larger share by itself.

sections.title: What markets did
sections.so_what: This book holds a chip designer at 8.6% and technology at 48%, so a day like Tuesday lands on it harder than on the average share.
evidence: On Tuesday 24 November the Philadelphia chip index fell 7.9% and the chip designer this book holds 5.9%
The same day the Dow rose 0.9% and retailers 2.3%: money moved from the suppliers of artificial intelligence to the shopper
Washington was reported to be preparing higher tariffs on its largest trading partners

sections.title: How markets are moving together
sections.so_what: This week, spreading across regions gives less cover than usual, and 86% of this book is in one of them.
evidence: The Tremor Index for the week of 20 November is Elevated, down from High the week before
US shares are moving with Europe’s and Taiwan’s far more closely than their norm of the past two years
Bonds, commodities and volatility carry most of the breaks; US industries against each other are calmer than usual

sections.title: The accounts in a past crash
sections.verdict: The cautious account is not cautious in a technology crash
sections.so_what: The three accounts are one book with three labels. Read them together.
evidence: A replay of the 2000 to 2002 crash: Capital Preservation −34%, Balanced −46%, Growth −61%
The largest position is 32% of Capital Preservation, 17% of Balanced and 24% of Growth
A replay of a past event on today’s holdings, not a forecast

sections.title: The dates ahead
sections.so_what: 8.6% of the book has its own event today: better known before than discovered after.
evidence: The chip designer reports results on 25 November after the US close
The October US inflation figure is due on 25 November
US retail sales for October are due on 27 November

links.text: The brief says money left the chip makers on Tuesday; the book shows 8.6% in one of them and 48% in technology. The news and the holdings are one story.
Regions are moving together more than usual, and 86% of the book is in one region: this week geography is not doing the spreading.
Exposure shows the same five holdings in all three accounts; the risk read shows what that does in a crash. The labels differ, the book does not.

watch: The chip designer’s results, 25 November after the US close
The October US inflation figure, 25 November
US retail sales for October, 27 November
The tariff plans the brief reports for China, the EU, Japan and South Korea
The next Tremor Index, for the week of 27 November
disclaimer: From Antevo answers, each dated. Shares of the whole, not amounts. A description of what the book holds, not advice to buy, sell or hold anything, and not a forecast.
